s: The architectural structure of which of the following temples exemplifies the independent style of the Chalukya-Cholas, incorporating Pallava and early Chalukya influences?
x:
The Draksharama Bhimeswara Temple represents the mature architectural style developed under the Chalukya-Cholas. Its design combines features of Pallava architecture, such as elegant structural planning, with Early Chalukyan elements, resulting in a distinctive regional style. This fusion later influenced temple architecture across the Godavari region. The Brihadeeshwara Temple at Thanjavur is a masterpiece of Imperial Chola architecture and does not represent the independent Chalukya-Chola style. The Padmakshi Temple at Hanamkonda is associated primarily with the Kakatiyas and reflects Kakatiya architectural traditions rather than Chalukya-Chola architecture. Therefore, Draksharama Temple is the correct answer.
Exam Note:

• Brihadeeshwara – Imperial Chola style

x: Vijnanesvara wrote the Dharmasastra Mitakshara based on the Yajnavalkya Smriti. Hindu property inheritance in India still follows Mitakshara.

s: Vijnanesvara wrote Mitakshara at the court of the Chalukya emperor Vikramaditya VI. It was
o: A commentary on the law book of Yajnavalkya
A commentary on the Arthashastra of Kautilya
x: The Mitakshara, written by Vijnanesvara at the court of Western Chalukya ruler Vikramaditya VI in the 12th century, is a commentary on the Yajnavalkya Smriti. It later formed the basis of the Mitakshara school of Hindu law.

s: Who is the author of Parashar Madhav, a commentary on the Parashara Smriti?
x: Parashar Madhav is Madhavacharya's commentary on the Parashara Smriti; Mitakshara is Vijnanesvara's and Chaturvarga Chintamani is Hemadri's.

s: Who is the author of the Dayabhaga?
x: Jimutavahana wrote the Dayabhaga; Vijnaneshwara wrote the Mitakshara and Hemadri the Chaturvarga Chintamani.

s: Who is the author of the legal digest Smriti Chandrika?
x: Devana Bhatta wrote Smriti Chandrika; Hemadri compiled Chaturvarga Chintamani and Ballal Sena wrote Daan Sagar.

s: Under the Dayabhaga system, when do sons acquire a right in ancestral property?
x: Dayabhaga recognises the sons' right in ancestral property only after the father's death, whereas Mitakshara gives it by birth.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Smriti Chandrika is associated with Devana Bhatta.
Parashar Madhav is associated with Devana Bhatta.
Smriti Chandrika is associated with Hindu law.
x: Option C is incorrect: Parashar Madhav is the work of Madhavacharya (Vidyaranya), not Devana Bhatta. Devana Bhatta wrote Smriti Chandrika on Hindu law, and Jimutavahana wrote Dayabhaga.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Mitakshara?
o: It is a commentary on the Yajnavalkya Smriti
Under it sons acquire a right in ancestral property by birth
It applied only to the upper castes
x: The claim that Mitakshara was for upper castes and Dayabhaga for lower castes is wrong; the other three statements are correct.

s: In which region does the Dayabhaga school of inheritance prevail?
x: Dayabhaga, by Jimutavahana, prevails in Bengal and Assam; the Mitakshara covers most of India.

s: Who is the author of the legal work Daan Sagar?
x: Daan Sagar was written by Ballal Sena; Devana Bhatta wrote Smriti Chandrika.

s: Parasara Madhaveeyam was the main law book for the administration of justice in which kingdom?
x: Madhavacharya's Parasara Madhaveeyam, a commentary on the Parashara Smriti, was the main law book of Vijayanagara justice.

s: On which Smriti is Madhavacharya's Parashar Madhav a commentary?
x: Parashar Madhav is a commentary on the Parashara Smriti; the Mitakshara is the commentary on the Yajnavalkya Smriti.

s: Who is the author of the Chaturvarga Chintamani?
x: Hemadri, a minister of the Yadavas of Devagiri, wrote the Chaturvarga Chintamani.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Kalyani Chalukya architecture used ornate pillars.
Kalyani Chalukya architecture featured undecorated doorways.
Kalyani Chalukya architecture included intricate wall motifs.
Kalyani Chalukya architecture included stepped superstructures.
x: Option B is incorrect: Kalyani Chalukya temples have richly decorated doorways, not plain ones. Ornate pillars, intricate wall motifs and stepped superstructures are all correct features.

s: Which stone was mainly used for Kalyani Chalukya temples of the mature Vesara (Gadag) style?
x: The Kalyani Chalukyas built mainly in chloritic schist (soapstone), not granite; their stellate plans later became a model for the Hoysalas.

s: How is the Itagi Mahadeva temple popularly described?
x: The Itagi Mahadeva temple is popularly known as the “Emperor among temples.”

s: Where is the Mahadeva temple of the Kalyani Chalukya period located?
x: The Mahadeva temple is at Itagi; Kasivishveshvara is at Lakkundi, Doddabasappa at Dambal and Kedareshwara at Balligavi.

s: Where is the Kasivishveshvara temple of the Kalyani Chalukya period located?
x: The Kasivishveshvara temple is at Lakkundi; Itagi has the Mahadeva temple and Dambal the Doddabasappa temple.

s: For which dynasty did the star-shaped (stellate) temple plans of the Kalyani Chalukyas later become a model?
x: The stellate plans of the Gadag style were later taken up as a model by the Hoysalas.

s: Where is the Doddabasappa temple of the Kalyani Chalukya period located?
x: The Doddabasappa temple is at Dambal; the Kedareshwara temple is at Balligavi.

s: According to the Khazipet inscription, with which event was the early rise of the Kakatiyas connected?
o: the conquest of Devagiri from the Yadavas
the founding of Dwarasamudra by the Hoysalas
the seizure of Kalyani by Bijjala
a grant of Hanamkonda with hereditary rights
x: The Khazipet inscription records Hanamkonda being granted with hereditary rights, reflecting the Kakatiyas’ rise as feudatories.

s: From which capital did the Yadavas (Seunas) rule after the weakening of the Kalyani Chalukyas?
x: The Yadavas or Seunas ruled from Devagiri; the Hoysalas from Dwarasamudra, the Kakatiyas from Hanamkonda-Warangal and the Kalachuris from Kalyani.

s: Who seized the throne at Kalyani around 1156 CE?
x: Kalachuri ruler Bijjala seized the throne at Kalyani around 1156 CE.

s: In which year did the Kalyani Chalukya dynasty come to an end?
x: The Kalyani Chalukyas ended around 1189 CE, and the Kakatiyas, Hoysalas and Yadavas emerged as successor powers.

s: Which was the capital of the Hoysalas, a successor power of the Kalyani Chalukyas?
x: The Hoysala capital was Dwarasamudra; the Yadavas ruled from Devagiri.

s: Which of the following pairs of successor powers and capitals is correctly matched?
x: The Kakatiyas ruled from Hanamkonda–Warangal; the Hoysalas ruled from Dwarasamudra, the Yadavas from Devagiri and the Kalachuris from Kalyani.
